LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 5.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: OUR TOURIST ATTRACTIONS Suggested Vocabulary big five, museum, attract, tour, pa
Topic 5.1: Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of OUR TOURIST ATTRACTIONS Suggested Vocabulary big five, museum, attract, tour, pa in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should we pronounce sounds correctly? 2. What information do we obtain when we listen keenly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  Listen to correct pronunciation of sounds, words, and phrases from the teacher, audio-visual recordings among others.  In purposive groups, work with peers to say words and phrases with the sounds /ð / and /θ / and assist one another,  Listen to a poem on tourist attraction sites in Kenya with various adverbial phrases such as proudly, in the park, by the river among others and recite it. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  Listen to correct pronunciation of sounds, words, and phrases from the teacher, audio-visual recordings among others.  In purposive groups, work with peers to say words and phrases with the sounds /ð / and /θ / and assist one another,  Listen to a poem on tourist attraction sites in Kenya with various adverbial phrases such as proudly, in the park, by the river among others and recite it. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Citizenship: The learner’s sense of patriotism is enhanced as they develop interest in socio-cultural and economic activities

by interacting with poems on Kenya’s tourist attraction sites.

 Self-efficacy: The learner’s ability to pay attention to detail is brought out as they use varied expressions in sentences to

express themselves.

Values:
Social justice is inculcated as the learner assists others to say words and phrases with the sounds /ð / and /θ/ without

discrimination.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Patriotism : The learner’s sense of patriotism is promoted as they are exposed to information on our tourist attraction sites by

listening to poems on the theme.

Link to other Subjects

The learner is able to relate the skills of pronouncing words correctly to the learning of sounds in Kiswahili.
